memory_update.text: NNI is the clean public reference for the node because it explicitly reports Loan Servicing and Systems plus Education Technology Services and Payments; later layers should separate servicing/payment economics from lending and asset-generation exposure.
MMS/Aidvantage is an underfollowed education-loan servicing infrastructure candidate hidden inside government-services/BPO; verify revenue materiality and contract performance risk before promotion.

RPAY is a speculative below-$300M exception: borrower-facing lender/servicer payment software is relevant to the workflow, but student-loan-specific customer evidence is still needed.

Private/non-listed chokepoint operators such as MOHELA, Edfinancial, TouchNet as a subsidiary, Transact Campus, TouchNet peers, and loan-servicing software vendors may be more operationally central than many public equities; public mapping may require parent-company or customer/supplier dependency analysis.

Servicing complexity creates a double-edged chokepoint: sticky contracts and compliance barriers can protect incumbents, but borrower communication failures, billing errors, and federal contract penalties are primary falsification risks.

node: Student-loan servicing, education payments, and borrower communications systems
summary: Expanded the universe around education loan servicing, campus payments, and borrower communications. The cleanest public-market reference is Nelnet because it directly reports Loan Servicing and Systems plus Education Technology Services and Payments. The underfollowed lane points to government-service operators, education-payment processors hidden inside broader payments companies, and sub-scale integrated-payment software vendors serving lenders/servicers. Key gating issue: separate recurring servicing/software/payment economics from credit exposure, political headline risk, and one-off contract penalties.
